summary.headline: Veefin H1 FY27 group revenue rose 116.2% to Rs 238.82 crore, with group PAT of Rs 24.85 crore and a 25.5% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Group revenue for H1 FY27 was Rs 238.82 crore, up 116.2% YoY, with group EBITDA of Rs 60.81 crore (25.5% margin) and PAT of Rs 24.85 crore (10.4% margin). Q2 revenue rose 9.2% QoQ to Rs 124.66 crore, and Q2 EBITDA margin was 29.4% versus 21.1% in Q1. Management reported an open pipeline of about Rs 920 crore with Rs 240 crore added in Q2, a new AI operating system (AIOS), and senior hires in delivery and customer roles. Operating cash flow was negative in H1, which management attributed to timing of billing and collections, and it expects H2 to improve.

segments.name: Standalone revenue mix
segments.commentary: Recurring fees were 82.1% of standalone H1 revenue and 89.8% in Q2. Existing customers contributed 73.9% of H1 revenue and 69.9% of Q2 revenue.

segments.name: Opportunity pipeline by product
segments.commentary: Supply chain finance about 35% of pipeline value, digital lending about 23%, trade and cash about 18%, digital banking about 16%, and fraud and risk in single digits. Geographically, about 84% is outside India (Southeast Asia, Middle East, Africa) and 16% in India.

segments.name: Subsidiary: White Rivers Media
segments.commentary: Consolidated for six months in H1 FY27 versus three months in H1 FY26, which management cited as a reason for the rise in cost of revenue. A DRHP listing filing is expected in January.

guidance_outlook: Management stated its EBITDA margin guidance range is 45% to 50%, and it is currently tracking above that range.
Management said it would not give formal forward guidance but expects its current revenue growth rate to continue for the next two years.
Management said product development spend is at the end of its cycle, and from next year essentially 99% will flow through the P&L rather than the balance sheet.
Management said no fresh debt or equity raise is planned; only already-sanctioned working capital lines will be drawn.
H2 is expected to be stronger on billing and collections, which management expects to reverse the H1 negative operating cash flow on a full-year basis.
capex_capacity: Veefin AIOS (AI operating system) has more than 1,000 reusable skills built, and three internal factories (implementation, support and testing) are running on it.
BSE in-principle approval for migration to the main board is in place; the NSE application is pending.
Voluntary adoption of Ind AS was made in preparation for the main board move, with restatement of past financials.
PSB Xchange: dealers onboarded, anchor approvals in place, AUM building; management declined to share revenue or AUM.
Hiring: Pavan (Chief Delivery Officer, ex-Tech Mahindra) and Akash Munjal (Chief Customer Officer) joined or were moved into roles in the last quarter.
demand_pricing: Open pipeline of about Rs 920 crore at the start of Q2, with about Rs 240 crore of net new opportunities added in the quarter.
About Rs 46 crore was contracted out of the pipeline in the quarter, and about Rs 35 crore was lost to deferrals or cancellations.
77 opportunities in the pipeline, of which 38 involve more than one product. About 75% of pipeline value is fully qualified, including about 11% under negotiation.
Management said new revenue drivers are a mix of existing-client revenue, new clients, and new product lines, with no geographic expansion planned.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue drivers for the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of existing-client revenue over contract periods, new client wins, and new product lines; no new geographies, with India a smaller part of the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product development expenses were reduced in H1 and that H1 product development spend was Rs 56-57 crore versus Rs 65 crore a year earlier; the balance-sheet capitalisation is ending, so 99% will flow through the P&L from next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from Q1 to Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 45-50% guided range is the reference, and quarterly fluctuations are expected; the current margin is above that range.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cash in hand low and how is liquidity managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital lines have been sanctioned but not fully drawn, as bank payments are expected at any time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Payal Maisheri said H1 cash flow lags P&L because of paying current and statutory liabilities, unbilled revenue and prepaid expenses. H2 billing is larger, and she expects the other current assets to turn positive over the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Will management share product-level metrics for PSB Xchange and other products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product-level revenue, AUM, or run-rate, citing competitive sensitivity and partner-bank requests, and said it will share company-level numbers only.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in H1 FY27, with DSO still at 88 days and a large unbilled revenue balance that must convert in H2.
Cash on hand was about Rs 0.56 crore at end-September, and undrawn working capital lines remain; the undrawn amount was not disclosed.
Pipeline is 84% outside India, and 65% sits outside supply chain finance; conversion of the Rs 920 crore pipeline (Rs 46 crore contracted in Q2) is the key test.
Q2 standalone and group EBITDA margins are above management's 45-50% range, and management flagged that margins will fluctuate.
Limited product-level disclosure (PSB Xchange, trade, lending) makes it hard for investors to track segment performance.
Amalgamation NCLT final hearing expected in November or December; WRM DRHP filing expected in January.
Investor queries on the FY25 fundraise were answered with Rs 160 crore (subsidiaries, Sep 2024) and Rs 88 crore (Veefin, Dec 2025) amounts, which management confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and margins, but evasive on product-level revenue, PSB Xchange metrics, undrawn debt and forward targets, citing competitive sensitivity and partner-bank restrictions. Management was cautious on cash flow, attributing negative operating cash flow to timing.
key_quotes: The first half has brought strong revenue growth and higher profits.
For H1, recurring fees represented 82.1% of revenue. In Q2, that share was 89.8%.
So, it's not 280, it's 88 that you should be looking at.
We are not going to go out and raise any more debt right now. Neither are we raising debt nor are we raising equity. No plans right now.
